headline: This 2021 law lets USAID use its logo and the U.S. flag to mark overseas programs and requires an audit of how partners follow branding rules.
what_it_does: The law allows the U.S. Agency for International Development to use markings, including its logo and the U.S. flag, to identify its overseas programs. Before this law, overseas programs were required to be identified as American Aid, and USAID guidelines allowed the flag only in certain situations. The USAID Inspector General must also send Congress an audit of whether partner organizations running USAID programs are following USAID branding requirements.

who_it_affects.how: The agency gains authority to use its logo and the U.S. flag to identify its overseas programs.

who_it_affects.group: Partner organizations that carry out USAID programs overseas
who_it_affects.how: They are subject to USAID branding requirements, and their compliance will be reviewed in an Inspector General audit.
The office must prepare and submit an audit of partner branding compliance to Congress.

who_it_affects.group: People in countries where USAID runs programs
who_it_affects.how: Overseas aid projects may display U.S. markings, including the flag, so the U.S. source of the aid may be more visible.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law January 13, 2021; the official summary does not list a separate effective date for its provisions.
